questions.q: What is SQL Server Data Tools (SSDT) today?
options: A workload you add to Visual Studio through the Visual Studio Installer
A standalone application, separate from Visual Studio, downloaded on its own
A feature that's automatically installed with every copy of SQL Server Management Studio
A command-line tool with no graphical interface
questions.explain: SSDT is installed as a component of Visual Studio itself, added through the Visual Studio Installer, not as a separate program.

questions.q: Where do you find the SQL Server Data Tools workload in the Visual Studio Installer?
options: Under the Data storage and processing toolset
Under Gaming
Under Office/SharePoint development
It isn't listed under Workloads at all
questions.explain: The SQL Server Data Tools checkbox appears under the Data storage and processing toolset in the Visual Studio Installer's Workloads tab.

questions.q: After installing the SSDT workload, why might the Integration Services Project template still be missing from New Project?
options: Because Integration Services ships as its own separate Visual Studio extension that has to be installed on top of SSDT
Because SSDT only works with SQL Server Management Studio, not Visual Studio
Because Integration Services projects require a paid Visual Studio license upgrade
The template can never be missing once SSDT is installed
questions.explain: Analysis Services, Integration Services, and Reporting Services each require their own separate extension, installed via Extensions > Manage Extensions or the Marketplace.

questions.q: What does the Integration Services Project template create when you select OK?
options: A new project containing a single, empty package (Package.dtsx by default)
A fully built ETL pipeline with sample data already loaded
Ten empty packages, one per common ETL scenario
Nothing until you manually add a package afterward
questions.explain: The Integration Services Project template creates a project that contains exactly one empty package, named Package.dtsx by default.

questions.q: Where do you create a new Integration Services project in Visual Studio?
options: File > New > Project, then select the Integration Services Project template
View > Toolbox
Tools > Options
Debug > Start Without Debugging
questions.explain: File > New > Project opens the New Project dialog, where you select the Integration Services Project template under Business Intelligence.
